correctness.rationale: The final claim is exactly finite through seven vertices. Complete recursive canonical augmentation yields 532 isomorphism classes with independent catalogue counts 1,1,2,4,12,56,456. Every out-neighborhood complex is reconstructed, every boundary-square relation is checked, and exact Smith normal forms show no homology invariant factor greater than 1. Mod-2 ranks independently agree with the free integral ranks. No inference is made beyond order seven.

originality.rationale: The inspected defining paper and extended abstract state that torsion in tournament neighborhood homology was unknown and do not provide the seven-vertex cutoff. Exact and alias searches found no stronger same-object statement. The nearest finite published-finding hit concerns arbitrary pure two-complexes, not complexes realizable as tournament out-neighborhood complexes. McKay supplies only the independent tournament census. The remaining risk is a later unindexed small-order computation under alternate directed-Hom terminology.
residual_risks: A later small-order computation may be unindexed or phrased only in directed-Hom terminology.
The originality conclusion is relative to the searches and inspected sources; it is not a proof that no unpublished or inaccessible computation exists.

value.rationale: The result advances an explicit open torsion question by proving the first nontrivial finite lower bound on the order of a torsion example: at least eight vertices. Seven is structurally motivated because the published \(2d+3\) construction first permits \(S^2\) tournament neighborhood topology at order seven, so this is the first \(H_2\)-capable order rather than an arbitrary census increment.
